home.title: Learn the method. Read both verdicts.
home.lede: Eight spoken lectures and a short film with each one. The six stages from the declassified training notes. A blind practice lab that scores a miss as carefully as a hit. Built from the SRI work, the Fort Meade program, and the 1995 evaluation — including the parts that say it was not useful.
home.recordBody: Utts: established, small to medium. Hyman: a real anomaly, an unnamed cause. AIR: not useful for intelligence. Timeline, the SAIC table, people, glossary, sources.

home.methodBody: Ideogram through model. Then seven lines to sort: write it as data, box it as AOL, or stop the session.

exclusions.title: What this course will not do
exclusions.lede: Five exclusions. Each one is a line, and a reason the line stays. The method is easy to point at a life. This course refuses that use.
course.title: Sound first. A short film beside each one.
course.lede: About twenty minutes, spoken. The films are ten seconds and start muted. Read along on the page, then answer two questions. Marking a lecture only means you heard it — the questions show their reasons either way.
lesson.filmCaption: A ten-second film for this lesson. It starts muted so it does not fight the lecture.
lesson.checkNote: Two questions. Wrong answers stay visible, with the reason.
journal.title: A record that can disappoint you
journal.lede: Scores stay on this device. After twenty sessions you have a rate. Before that, you have a mood.
lab.title: A blind page
lab.lede: Ten minutes. Ideogram, four senses, one sketch. The picture stays off this page until you seal it. The seal is a discipline, not a lock.
lab.step1: 1. Take the cue. Do not try to decode it. It does not describe the target.
lab.step2: 2. One mark. Write A, the feeling. Write B from the small vocabulary, or box an AOL.
lab.step3: 3. Temperature, texture, sound, light. Then masses and how they sit.
lab.step4: 4. Seal. Then look. Then score the miss as carefully as the hit.
lab.pool: Places and objects in this pool only — {{count}} targets, chosen so recent ones wait their turn. People, medicine, legal claims, money, and borrowed stamps are excluded. The reasons are under the page.
lab.cueNote: Cue only. It is not a coordinate and it is not a hint.
lab.stage2: Stage II · temperature, texture, sound, light
lab.stage3: Stage III · masses and how they sit
lab.aolPlaceholder: If a name arrived, write it here and leave it
lab.sealedNote: The page is closed. Opening the target is feedback. If you already knew which picture this was, mark the session contaminated and do not count it.
lab.scoreNote: Score only what you wrote before this picture. Adjacency is not a hit.
lab.scoreSensory: At least two sensory lines match
lab.lockedZero: Locked at {{hits}} of 3. A zero is data.
lab.lockedStrong: Locked at {{hits}} of 3. A strong training page.
lab.lockedMixed: Locked at {{hits}} of 3. Mixed. Keep it mixed.
lab.modelNote: A clean stage I–III line for this target, written after the fact so it cannot help you: {{model}}
lab.drawError: The score is saved. The drawings could not be stored on this device.

method.title: Six stages. Low information first.
method.lede: The declassified stage chart runs from a major gestalt to a three-dimensional model. The working rule between them is the same: objectify, and do not let a noun drive.
method.nounsTitle: The only legal nouns at stage I
method.nounsNote: Anything more specific is analytical overlay until feedback says otherwise.
method.sortLede: Seven things a viewer might write. Decide before you read the reason.
method.overlayNote: Overlay is a writing rule. The course also refuses five uses of the method itself — people, medicine, legal claims, money, and borrowed stamps.
archive.title: What was claimed, and what the evaluation refused.
archive.lede: Remote viewing, here, means the SRI and military program that ended in 1995, plus the method that program trained. The primary papers disagree with each other. This page keeps the disagreement.
archive.saicNote: As listed by Jessica Utts from figures Edwin May supplied to the review team in a memorandum of 25 July 1995. Effect size near zero is chance. These six are the remote-viewing experiments in that list of ten. The spread is the point: a small effect does not win every study.
archive.effectNote: Five-choice effect size, from Utts: (3 − average rank) / √2. Small 0.2 is an average rank near 2.72. Medium 0.5 is near 2.29. Chance is 3.
archive.peopleNote: Roles, not halos. Commercial teachers after 1995 are a separate literature from the evaluation.
archive.sourcesTitle: Read the paper, not the retelling
archive.sourcesNote: The method was claimed as proprietary to Swann. It was not granted as a patent. Puthoff’s patents are about communications, not viewing.
faq.title: Sources, patents, and the pass.
faq.lede: The academy is built. The method was claimed as proprietary. It was not granted as a patent. The papers are listed twice: here, short, and on the record, with the limits.
